title: Measure callouts move out of the way instead of covering what they measure
goal: An alignment check reading off 5 px is drawn in the middle of its own guide, which lands directly on top of the misaligned label it is judging, so the one element you need to look at is the one hidden. Every callout the measure tools draw should sit in nearby whitespace and stay clearly attached to its subject, so a measurement never destroys the evidence for its own claim.
notes: Playtest 2026-08-23, screenshot attached to the feedback. Root cause: MeasureRasterizer.drawAlignmentCheck places the chip at g.labelAnchor, the feet-line midpoint, which for an edge-alignment guide is by construction on top of the elements being checked. The guide is drawn split around the chip, so the geometry already assumes the chip sits ON the line. Options worth weighing in the adversarial review: place the chip just beyond the guide end that has canvas room; or offset it perpendicular to the guide, away from the side the checked elements occupy. The principle now lives in shared/UX-PATTERNS.md D14 and covers all annotations, not just this chip, so fix the family rather than the instance. Do not regress the split-guide look if the chip moves off the line: it may no longer need splitting.
acceptance: The alignment verdict chip sits clear of every element the guide is checking, and the outlier stays fully visible
Caliper value chips, gap labels and the role legend also avoid covering the thing they describe
A relocated callout still reads as belonging to its subject, by adjacency or a leader line
Two measurements close together nudge their labels apart rather than stacking them
Moving a label never moves the guide, ticks or connector: the geometry stays exactly where the measurement is
Verified on the test capture: covering each callout with a thumb still leaves everything it claims visible
